title: Nahum Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Nahum chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Nahum Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Nahum Chapter 3.

questions.question: What is the condition of the city mentioned in Nahum 3:1?
options: It is full of lies and robbery
It is a place of worship
questions.correctAnswer: It is full of lies and robbery
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:1 states that the city is full of lies and robbery, indicating its violent and deceitful nature.

questions.question: Which sound is NOT mentioned in Nahum 3:2?
questions.correctAnswer: The sound of trumpets
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:2 mentions the noise of a whip, rattling wheels, pransing horses, and jumping chariots, but does not mention trumpets.

questions.question: What do the horsemen lift up in Nahum 3:3?
questions.correctAnswer: Bright sword and glittering spear
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:3 clearly states the horseman lifteth up both the bright sword and the glittering spear.

questions.question: According to Nahum 3:4, what does the wellfavoured harlot sell through her witchcrafts?
questions.correctAnswer: Nations and families
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:4 describes the harlot as selling nations through her whoredoms and families through her witchcrafts.

questions.question: Who declares judgment against the city in Nahum 3:5?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD of hosts
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:5 states that the LORD of hosts declares He is against the city and will reveal its shame.

questions.question: What will happen to the city as described in Nahum 3:6?
options: It will be cast with abominable filth and made vile
It will be exalted and blessed
It will be rebuilt and prosper
It will be protected by angels
questions.correctAnswer: It will be cast with abominable filth and made vile
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:6 says the city will have abominable filth cast upon it, will be made vile, and become a gazingstock.

questions.question: What will people say when they see the city in Nahum 3:7?
options: Nineveh is laid waste: who will bemoan her?
Nineveh is a city of peace
questions.correctAnswer: Nineveh is laid waste: who will bemoan her?
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:7 describes people fleeing and saying that Nineveh is laid waste and questioning who will bemoan her.

questions.question: True or False: Nahum 3:8 compares the city to populous No which was surrounded by rivers and seas.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:8 explicitly compares the city to populous No that was situated among rivers and had waters all around it.

questions.question: True or False: According to Nahum 3:9, Ethiopia and Egypt were enemies of the city.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:9 states Ethiopia and Egypt were the city's strength, not enemies.

questions.question: What happened to the young children of the city according to Nahum 3:10?
options: They were dashed in pieces at the top of all the streets
They were hidden in secret places
questions.correctAnswer: They were dashed in pieces at the top of all the streets
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:10 states the young children were dashed in pieces at the top of all the streets.

questions.question: According to Nahum 3:11, what will the city also experience?
options: It shall be drunken and hidden
It shall be exalted and praised
It shall be fortified and strong
It shall be peaceful and quiet
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be drunken and hidden
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:11 says the city shall be drunken and hidden and will seek strength because of the enemy.

questions.question: True or False: Nahum 3:12 compares the city's strong holds to fig trees with firstripe figs.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:12 uses the metaphor of fig trees with firstripe figs to describe the fragile nature of the city's strong holds.

questions.question: True or False: Nahum 3:13 says the gates of the city shall be strongly guarded and closed to enemies.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:13 states the gates shall be set wide open to enemies, not strongly guarded.

questions.question: In Nahum 3, which comes first?
options: The noise of chariots and horses
The casting of abominable filth upon the city
The gates of the city being set wide open
The city being drunken and seeking strength
questions.correctAnswer: The noise of chariots and horses
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:2 mentions the noise of the whip, wheels, horses, and chariots before the other events occur later in the chapter.

questions.question: What will happen to the city's bars according to Nahum 3:13?
options: They shall be devoured by fire
They shall be reinforced with iron
They shall be made of gold
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be devoured by fire
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:13 says the fire shall devour the bars of the city.

medium.title: Nahum Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Nahum Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Nahum 3:8, which city is compared to Nineveh for its populous nature and natural defenses?
questions.correctAnswer: No
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:8 specifically compares Nineveh to populous No, highlighting its location among rivers and natural water defenses.

questions.question: Which nations are mentioned as the strength and helpers of No in Nahum 3:9?
questions.correctAnswer: Ethiopia, Egypt, Put, Lubim
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:9 lists Ethiopia and Egypt as the strength of No and Put and Lubim as its helpers.

questions.question: What tragic fate befell the young children and honorable men of No as described in Nahum 3:10?
options: Children dashed in pieces; honorable men bound in chains
questions.correctAnswer: Children dashed in pieces; honorable men bound in chains
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:10 describes how the young children were dashed in pieces at the street tops and honorable men were bound in chains.

questions.question: Based on Nahum 3:11, what condition will Nineveh experience as a result of facing its enemy?
questions.correctAnswer: Drunkenness and hiding, seeking strength
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:11 predicts that Nineveh will be drunken and hidden, and will seek strength because of the enemy.

questions.question: How does Nahum 3:12 describe the fate of Nineveh's strongholds?
options: Like fig trees with unripe figs, falling into the mouth of the eater
Like castles on the sea, invincible
questions.correctAnswer: Like fig trees with unripe figs, falling into the mouth of the eater
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:12 compares Nineveh's strongholds to fig trees with early figs that fall when shaken, symbolizing their fragility.

questions.question: What does Nahum 3:13 say about the people of Nineveh and the security of their gates?
options: Their people are women; gates open to enemies; fire devours bars
Their people are warriors; gates are sealed; no fire
Their people are merchants; gates guarded; bars strong
Their people are kings; gates closed; bars intact
questions.correctAnswer: Their people are women; gates open to enemies; fire devours bars
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:13 states that the people are women, the gates will be open to enemies, and fire will devour the bars, showing vulnerability.

questions.question: What practical steps does Nahum 3:14 advise for a city under siege?
options: Draw waters, fortify strongholds, tread mortar, strengthen brickkiln
Build more walls, train soldiers, increase food supplies, pray
Send envoys, negotiate peace, gather armies, fast
Hide valuables, flee city, burn fields, surrender
questions.correctAnswer: Draw waters, fortify strongholds, tread mortar, strengthen brickkiln
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:14 instructs to prepare for siege by securing water, strengthening fortifications, and making bricks stronger.

questions.question: How does Nahum 3:15 use the imagery of the cankerworm and locusts to describe the destruction of Nineveh?
options: The sword and fire will devour like cankerworms; increase like locusts
The city will flourish like crops after rain
The people will be as numerous as stars
The enemies will flee like scattered birds
questions.correctAnswer: The sword and fire will devour like cankerworms; increase like locusts
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:15 compares the destructive sword and fire to cankerworms and locusts that consume everything, emphasizing total ruin.

questions.question: What lesson about pride and trust in worldly alliances can we learn from Nahum 3:9-10?
options: Relying on allies is futile as even strong nations are carried into captivity
Strength in numbers always ensures security
Captivity can be avoided by military might alone
questions.correctAnswer: Relying on allies is futile as even strong nations are carried into captivity
questions.explanation: Verses 9 and 10 show that despite the strength from allies, No was taken captive, teaching that trust in worldly power is unreliable.

questions.question: True or False: Nahum 3:12 teaches that even the strongest defenses can fail if shaken.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:12 compares strongholds to fig trees with early figs that fall if shaken, illustrating the vulnerability of defenses.

questions.question: True or False: Nahum 3:13 depicts the people of Nineveh as strong warriors ready to defend their city gates.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:13 states that the people are women and the gates will be open to enemies, indicating weakness rather than strength.

questions.question: What is the connection between Nahum 3:14 and Nahum 3:15 regarding the city's preparations and ultimate fate?
options: Despite preparations to fortify, fire and sword will still devour the city
Preparations will ensure the city's long-lasting victory
The city will be saved by drawing waters and building brickkilns
The enemy will be deterred by strong fortifications
questions.correctAnswer: Despite preparations to fortify, fire and sword will still devour the city
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:14 describes efforts to prepare for siege, but 3:15 warns that fire and sword will consume the city regardless, showing the futility of such defenses.

questions.question: According to Nahum 3:18, what is the condition of the shepherds, nobles, and people of Nineveh during its downfall?
options: Shepherds slumber, nobles dwell in dust, people scattered on mountains
Shepherds lead bravely, nobles stand firm, people united
Shepherds flee, nobles conquer, people celebrate
Shepherds sing, nobles rejoice, people gather
questions.correctAnswer: Shepherds slumber, nobles dwell in dust, people scattered on mountains
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:18 depicts a scene of neglect and defeat where leaders are inactive and the people are scattered and abandoned.

questions.question: What does Nahum 3:19 reveal about Nineveh's wound and the reaction of those who hear about it?
options: The wound is grievous and unhealed; all clap hands over her
The wound is minor; people pray for her healing
The wound is hidden; people ignore her plight
The wound is healing; people rejoice for her recovery
questions.correctAnswer: The wound is grievous and unhealed; all clap hands over her
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:19 states that Nineveh's wound is grievous and without healing, causing all who hear to clap hands in approval of her judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Nahum 3:11 indicates that Nineveh will seek strength because of the enemy but will ultimately be victorious.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:11 says Nineveh will seek strength because of the enemy but in context of the chapter, this seeking is in vain and leads to downfall.

hard.title: Nahum Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Nahum Chapter 3.

questions.question: According to Nahum 3:15, what will devour Nineveh along with the sword?
questions.correctAnswer: The fire
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:15 states, 'There shall the fire devour thee; the sword shall cut thee off...', indicating that fire will devour Nineveh along with the sword.

questions.question: In Nahum 3:16, to what does the prophet compare the multitude of merchants?
questions.correctAnswer: Stars of heaven
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:16 states, 'Thou hast multiplied thy merchants above the stars of heaven,' directly comparing the merchants to stars in the sky.

questions.question: What insect imagery is used in Nahum 3:17 to describe the crowned and captains of Nineveh?
questions.correctAnswer: Locusts and grasshoppers
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:17 describes, 'Thy crowned are as the locusts, and thy captains as the great grasshoppers,' using locust and grasshopper imagery.

questions.question: What happens to the nobles of Assyria according to Nahum 3:18?
options: They shall dwell in the dust
They shall flee to the mountains
questions.correctAnswer: They shall dwell in the dust
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:18 says, 'thy nobles shall dwell in the dust,' indicating their downfall and humiliation.

questions.question: How does Nahum 3:19 describe the wound of Nineveh?
questions.correctAnswer: Grievous and without healing
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:19 states, 'There is no healing of thy bruise; thy wound is grievous,' emphasizing the severity and permanence of Nineveh's judgment.

questions.question: Which phrase in Nahum 3:15 uses a simile to illustrate destruction?
options: 'It shall eat thee up like the cankerworm'
questions.correctAnswer: 'It shall eat thee up like the cankerworm'
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:15 contains the simile 'it shall eat thee up like the cankerworm,' comparing destruction to a devouring insect.

questions.question: In Nahum 3:16, what action does the cankerworm do?
questions.correctAnswer: Spoileth and flieth away
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:16 says, 'the cankerworm spoileth, and flieth away,' describing its destructive and fleeting nature.

questions.question: What does Nahum 3:18 say about the people of Assyria?
options: They are scattered upon the mountains
They are united in the city
questions.correctAnswer: They are scattered upon the mountains
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:18 states, 'thy people is scattered upon the mountains, and no man gathereth them,' showing their dispersion and abandonment.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book also uses locust imagery to symbolize destruction and judgment, connecting with Nahum 3:15-17?
questions.correctAnswer: Joel
questions.explanation: The book of Joel (Joel 1:4) uses locusts to symbolize devastating judgment, paralleling the locust and cankerworm imagery in Nahum 3:15-17.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'cankerworm' in Nahum 3:15 likely refers to what kind of creature?
questions.correctAnswer: A destructive larva or locust
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term for 'cankerworm' (arbeh) in Nahum 3:15 refers to an insect larva or locust known for destruction, highlighting the metaphor of devastation.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Nahum 3:17 when describing the crowned and captains as locusts and grasshoppers?
questions.correctAnswer: Simile
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:17 uses a simile by comparing leaders to locusts and grasshoppers, using 'as' to highlight their fleeting and insignificant nature.

questions.question: What is the significance of the imagery of 'shepherds slumbering' in Nahum 3:18 in the context of ancient Near Eastern kingship?
options: It symbolizes neglect of leadership and vulnerability
It indicates peaceful rest after victory
It means the king is asleep physically
It shows the shepherds are protected
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes neglect of leadership and vulnerability
questions.explanation: In Nahum 3:18, 'thy shepherds slumber' metaphorically represents leaders neglecting duties, leading to vulnerability and downfall, common in ancient Near Eastern leadership imagery.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of Nineveh's destruction as a warning to repentance, connecting with Nahum's message?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 12:41
questions.explanation: Matthew 12:41 references 'the men of Nineveh' repenting at Jonah's preaching, echoing Nahum's theme of Nineveh's judgment and call to repentance.

questions.question: True or False: Nahum 3:19 declares that all who hear about Nineveh's destruction will mourn deeply over her fall.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:19 states, 'all that hear the bruit of thee shall clap the hands over thee,' indicating rejoicing, not mourning, over Nineveh's destruction.

questions.question: True or False: Nahum 3:14 advises strengthening defenses by drawing water for the siege and fortifying strongholds.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:14 commands to 'Draw thee waters for the siege, fortify thy strong holds,' indicating preparation for defense.

theological.title: Nahum Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Nahum Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Nahum 3:1, what characterizes the 'bloody city'?
options: Full of lies and robbery with continuous prey
Known for its peace and justice
A city of worship and righteousness
A city protected by divine angels
questions.correctAnswer: Full of lies and robbery with continuous prey
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:1 describes the city as full of lies and robbery, and that the prey departeth not, indicating ongoing violence and corruption.

questions.question: What imagery is used in Nahum 3:2 to depict the city's impending destruction?
options: The noise of a whip, rattling wheels, prancing horses, and jumping chariots
The sound of peaceful rivers and gentle winds
The silence of an abandoned city
questions.correctAnswer: The noise of a whip, rattling wheels, prancing horses, and jumping chariots
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:2 uses vivid war imagery including the noise of a whip, rattling wheels, prancing horses, and jumping chariots to symbolize the approaching siege.

questions.question: What does Nahum 3:4 reveal about the cause of Nineveh's downfall?
options: Whoredoms and witchcrafts leading to the selling of nations and families
questions.correctAnswer: Whoredoms and witchcrafts leading to the selling of nations and families
questions.explanation: Verse 4 identifies Nineveh's moral corruption—whoredoms and witchcrafts—as the reason for its downfall, emphasizing spiritual and ethical decay.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Nahum 3:5 where God declares opposition to Nineveh?
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice and righteous judgment
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:5 shows God's justice as He declares opposition to Nineveh and intends to expose its shame and nakedness.

questions.question: What is the effect of God's judgment on Nineveh as described in Nahum 3:7?
options: All who look upon Nineveh shall flee and lament its destruction
Nineveh will be strengthened and defended
The nations will unite to comfort Nineveh
Nineveh will rise again like a phoenix
questions.correctAnswer: All who look upon Nineveh shall flee and lament its destruction
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:7 states that all who see the city will flee and ask who will mourn Nineveh, indicating total desolation and abandonment.

questions.question: How does Nahum 3:8-9 contrast Nineveh's former strength with its coming fall?
options: Though once protected by rivers, seas, and allies like Ethiopia and Egypt, it will fall into captivity
Nineveh was always weak despite its allies
Nineveh's strength was solely due to its military power
The city's strength was spiritual rather than political
questions.correctAnswer: Though once protected by rivers, seas, and allies like Ethiopia and Egypt, it will fall into captivity
questions.explanation: Verses 8-9 highlight Nineveh's formidable natural and political defenses and allies, yet despite this, it faces inevitable captivity.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sinfulness and divine judgment is taught by the combination of Nahum 3:10 and 3:19?
options: Persistent wickedness leads to grievous wounds without healing, resulting in public shame
Human sinfulness is easily forgiven without consequences
Divine punishment is temporary and minor
Sinfulness is unrelated to national downfall
questions.correctAnswer: Persistent wickedness leads to grievous wounds without healing, resulting in public shame
questions.explanation: Nahum 3:10 describes captivity and violent judgment, while 3:19 states the wound has no healing and wickedness continually passes, teaching the doctrine of the consequences of persistent sin.

questions.question: What does Nahum 3:11 teach about the condition of Nineveh in the face of its enemies?
options: It will be drunken, hidden, and will seek strength in vain
It will triumph and destroy its enemies
It will remain fearless and unshaken
questions.correctAnswer: It will be drunken, hidden, and will seek strength in vain
questions.explanation: Verse 11 metaphorically describes Nineveh as drunken and hiding, indicating weakness and desperation against its enemies.

questions.question: What theological insight about divine sovereignty and human defenses is communicated in Nahum 3:12-13?
options: Human strongholds are fragile and vulnerable to God's judgment, even when heavily fortified
Human defenses are sufficient against all threats
God only judges individuals, not cities
questions.correctAnswer: Human strongholds are fragile and vulnerable to God's judgment, even when heavily fortified
questions.explanation: Verses 12-13 depict strongholds likened to fig trees easily shaken and gates opened to enemies, showing that human defenses cannot withstand God's judgment.

questions.question: According to Nahum 3:14, what preparations does Nineveh make for the siege, and what does this reveal about human effort in the face of divine judgment?
options: Drawing water, fortifying strongholds, and making bricks, yet these efforts are ultimately futile
Making peace treaties to avoid conflict
questions.correctAnswer: Drawing water, fortifying strongholds, and making bricks, yet these efforts are ultimately futile
questions.explanation: Verse 14 describes human efforts to prepare defenses, but the chapter context shows these are insufficient against God's judgment.

questions.question: What symbolic imagery in Nahum 3:15-16 is used to describe the consuming nature of God's judgment on Nineveh?
options: Fire consuming like the cankerworm and locusts spoiling and flying away
A gentle rain nurturing the land
questions.correctAnswer: Fire consuming like the cankerworm and locusts spoiling and flying away
questions.explanation: Verses 15-16 employ imagery of destructive locusts and fire to symbolize the thorough and consuming nature of divine judgment.

questions.question: What does Nahum 3:17 imply about the leadership and stability of Nineveh?
options: Its leaders are unstable and flee at the first sign of danger
Its leaders are strong and unyielding
Its leaders are wise and courageous
Its leaders are divinely appointed and protected
questions.correctAnswer: Its leaders are unstable and flee at the first sign of danger
questions.explanation: Verse 17 compares crowned leaders to locusts and captains to grasshoppers that flee at sunrise, implying instability and lack of courage.

questions.question: How does Nahum 3:18 describe the condition of Nineveh's people and leaders, and what does this teach about the consequences of sin on social order?
options: Shepherds sleep, nobles dwell in dust, and the people are scattered without gathering
Leaders lead wisely and people remain united
The city prospers under strong governance
The people are protected and gathered in peace
questions.correctAnswer: Shepherds sleep, nobles dwell in dust, and the people are scattered without gathering
questions.explanation: Verse 18 depicts failure of leadership and social disintegration due to sin and judgment, illustrating societal collapse.

questions.question: What combined teaching about God's justice and the certainty of punishment can be drawn from Nahum 3:5-6 and Nahum 3:19?
options: God's judgment is just and inescapable, resulting in grievous wounds that have no healing
God's judgment is easily avoided by repentance alone
God shows partiality and allows some wickedness to flourish
God's punishment is temporary and easily forgotten
questions.correctAnswer: God's judgment is just and inescapable, resulting in grievous wounds that have no healing
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 declare God's opposition and exposing of shame, while 3:19 describes wounds without healing, teaching the doctrine of inescapable divine justice.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s judgment in Nahum 3 is an example of divine cruelty. What does Nahum 3:7-10 actually teach about the nature and purpose of God's judgment?
options: God’s judgment serves as righteous retribution for persistent wickedness and corruption
God’s judgment is unjust and unprovoked
God’s judgment is a myth with no real effect
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment serves as righteous retribution for persistent wickedness and corruption
questions.explanation: Verses 7-10 describe Nineveh’s ruin as a consequence of its violence and sin, showing God’s judgment as just retribution, not cruelty.
